node.label: T. M. Devine
node.description: A historian of Scottish society, economy and diaspora. The Tobacco Lords (1975) studied Glasgow’s tobacco merchants, Clanship to Crofters’ War (1994) the social transformation of the Highlands, and The Scottish Nation (1999) is his history of modern Scotland. In ‘Did Slavery Make Scotia Great?’ (2011) he reopens Eric Williams’s question about slavery and economic development, arguing that Scotland’s stake cannot be measured by the few slaving voyages from its ports but must include the wider plantation economies. With Jenny Wormald he called for comparative, internationalized Scottish history rather than an insular national narrative.
